title: Everyday Exchanges
description: After this level you can handle the routine situations of daily life in Tagalog: talk about your work, studies and background in some depth, narrate your day in order, ask for and give directions around town, describe symptoms at a pharmacy or clinic, compare people and things, make and politely decline invitations, and tell simple stories about past experiences. Grammatically, you break through the biggest hurdle of the language: the focus system. You learn to say the same event with actor focus (mag-/-um-) or object focus (-in), meet the locative -an and benefactive i- verbs, master all three aspects plus the recently-completed kaka- form, and season your speech with the little particles — na, pa, lang, din, daw, naman — that make Tagalog sound like Tagalog.
canDo: I can describe my job, studies and nationality and ask others about theirs.
I can say who something is for and use the full set of sa-pronouns (akin, iyo, kaniya...).
I can talk about the same event with actor focus or object focus and choose the natural one.
I can narrate my day in order using una, tapos, pagkatapos and bago.
I can say what I can do, may do, must do and must not do.
I can invite someone to do something, accept, or decline politely.
I can ask for and give simple directions and get around town.
I can describe symptoms and manage a visit to a pharmacy or doctor.
I can compare people and things and describe personality and appearance.
I can talk about past experiences, give reasons with kasi, and make simple future plans.
